planting.note: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost and transplant into deep, well-worked beds once soil has warmed.

directions: Delicious is an old Burpee introduction famous for producing some of the largest tomato fruit of any variety, including the fruit that held the Guinness World Record for heaviest tomato for nearly three decades. Stake or cage plants heavily and prune to a few main leaders so the vigorous indeterminate vines can channel energy into fewer, larger scarlet-red beefsteak fruits. Consistent deep watering and calcium availability help reduce cracking and blossom end rot on fruit that can exceed a pound. Choose this variety when garden bragging rights and classic rich tomato flavor matter more than earliness or disease-package breadth.

planting.note: Transplant after all danger of frost once soil has warmed, spacing plants generously for good airflow around the semi-determinate vines.

directions: BHN 589 is a widely grown Southeastern hybrid valued by market growers and home gardeners for combining excellent flavor with a strong resistance package to Fusarium wilt races 1 and 2, Verticillium wilt, and tobacco mosaic virus. Semi-determinate vines set heavy clusters of crack-resistant 8-10 ounce fruit that hold shelf life well after picking. Stake or cage for support and maintain even soil moisture to minimize splitting during the humid summer fruit set. Choose this variety where disease pressure is high but you still want dependable, large-fruited flavor rather than a purely commercial round tomato.

planting.note: Transplant into full sun after frost danger passes and stake early since the indeterminate vines carry unusually heavy paste fruit.

directions: Big Mama produces oversized plum-shaped fruit up to five inches long, far larger than a typical Roma or San Marzano, while keeping the dense, low-seed flesh needed for thick sauce and paste. The indeterminate vines need sturdy staking and steady watering to support the heavy fruit load without splitting. Its meaty walls and easy-peel skin make it a favorite for home canners who want fewer tomatoes to process a given volume of sauce. Pick this cultivar when you want paste-tomato texture in a fruit large enough to slice and eat fresh as well.

planting.note: Transplant compact determinate plants after last frost; little to no staking is needed given the tidy, self-supporting habit.

directions: Health Kick is a determinate saladette-paste hybrid bred by Seminis to concentrate roughly 50 percent more lycopene than a standard tomato while keeping a broad disease-resistance package that includes Fusarium wilt, Verticillium wilt, tomato spotted wilt virus, and bacterial speck. Compact plants stay under three feet and need only minimal caging, making them well suited to smaller raised-bed plantings. The 3-5 ounce cylindrical fruits work equally well diced fresh, roasted, or cooked into sauce. Choose this variety when disease resistance and nutritional density matter as much as culinary versatility.

planting.note: Transplant after frost danger and stake or cage the vigorous indeterminate vines early for support.

directions: Black Opal is a modern English open-pollinated selection bred from Black Cherry for a firmer texture and sweeter flavor than its parent, ripening to a deep chocolate-black skin over dusky red flesh. Indeterminate vines are early and heavy-yielding, producing clusters of half-to-one-ounce fruit through the season on a slightly more compact growth habit than many dark cherry types. Regular even watering and full sun bring out the complex, well-balanced sweetness the variety is known for. Select this cultivar for gardeners who want the dark cherry-tomato flavor profile with improved earliness and cracking resistance.

planting.note: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost and stake the tall indeterminate vines well at transplant.

directions: Federle, also called Federle's Italian Paste, is an heirloom preserved through Seed Savers Exchange that produces unusually long, slender paste fruit up to seven inches, distinct from the more common blocky Roma shape. Indeterminate vines are highly productive and keep setting fruit steadily through the season, so gardeners canning or making salsa get an extended harvest window rather than one heavy flush. The dense, nearly seedless flesh cooks down quickly with little waste, and the deep red color holds well in finished sauce. Grow this variety when you want an open-pollinated, seed-saveable paste tomato with a distinctive elongated shape for home preserving.
